title: Turkey, thigh, cooked, skin not eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Turkey is a domesticated bird, and its thigh meat is high in protein and low in fat, especially after the skin is removed. Cooked turkey thigh is commonly used in salads, soups, and quick‑prep dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turkey thigh meat contains more iron than chicken breast.
Turkeys were domesticated in North America over 2,000 years ago.
In the United States, turkey is the traditional centerpiece for Thanksgiving.
When boiled without skin, the fat content drops to less than 2 %.
Turkey belongs to the pheasant family, along with chickens and pheasants.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving of cooked, skin‑less turkey thigh provides about 30 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Removing the skin makes the product virtually fat‑free, suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports red blood cell formation and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of zinc and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals help maintain immune function and antioxidant protection.

items.title: Supports bone health
items.content: Turkey provides phosphorus and a modest amount of calcium, both important for bone tissue.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to bird meat.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked turkey can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; proper cooking temperatures are essential.

items.title: High sodium if salted
items.content: If the product is seasoned with salt, monitor sodium intake, especially for hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skin‑less turkey thigh can be diced for salads, added to soups and stews, or used in sandwiches. It reheats quickly in the microwave or on a skillet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep refrigerated at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container for 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze at ‑18 °C for up to 2‑3 months.
